book-backwater.intro: Backwater is an Australian post-apocalyptic novel about a water carrier crossing a water-scarce landscape. Its story follows the strain of survival, grief and exhaustion, and the difficult choices that can let isolated communities cooperate.

details.heading: A journey shaped by water
details.text: Water is scarce, the journey is exhausting, and the people along the way have their own grief to carry. Backwater follows the work of surviving and finding a way to keep going. There is also an early game prototype based on the novel; it is a separate project.

details.heading: Reading editions
details.text: I announced Backwater on Amazon on 1 May 2026 in Kindle Unlimited, Kindle ebook, paperback and hardcover editions. Check Amazon for the editions currently available in your region.

faqs.question: Which reading formats were announced?
faqs.answer: The 1 May 2026 announcement included Kindle Unlimited, Kindle ebook, paperback and hardcover editions. Check Amazon for current availability in your region.

faqs.question: Is Backwater also a game?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is an early game prototype based on the novel. The book and prototype are separate projects, so choose the book link if you want to read the story.

updates.dateMeaning: Date of the author's announcement that the book was available on Amazon
updates.title: Backwater announced for Amazon editions
updates.summary: I announced Backwater on Amazon in Kindle Unlimited, Kindle ebook, paperback and hardcover editions.

book-toknight.intro: ToKnight is a middle-grade fantasy adventure about Jason Proud, a Year Six student who is drawn into a real knightly duty. A spectral ancestor gives him armour, a shield and a sword, then warns that an ancient dragon is returning and feeds on fear, anger, shame and pain.

details.heading: Courage beyond the armour
details.text: Jason still has school, family, friends and a bully to deal with while the danger grows. Being a knight means learning to help someone even when they are the last person he wants to help.

details.heading: For readers
details.text: Recommended for readers aged 9–12, and older readers who enjoy funny, layered middle-grade fantasy. Follow the Amazon link to read it; the itch.io page is a showcase, not a book download.

faqs.question: Who is ToKnight for?
faqs.answer: Ages 9–12, as well as older readers who enjoy funny, layered middle-grade fantasy.

faqs.question: Can I download the book from itch.io?
faqs.answer: No. You can read about the book on itch.io, but the book itself is available through the linked Amazon page.

book-article-18.intro: Article 18 is an adult comic-noir mystery novella about Austin Crowd, a private investigator whose instinct for patterns often leads him toward the wrong explanation. A sealed packet draws him into a tangle of missing records, political manoeuvring, polite threats and questions people would rather he stopped asking.

details.heading: A case that keeps changing shape
details.text: Austin works through offices, receptions and back channels with help from Jules, who is not impressed by his methods. His confident misreadings cause almost as much trouble as the people trying to silence him.

details.heading: Choose an edition
details.text: Download the PDF or EPUB from itch.io on a name-your-price basis. Google Play has a 135-page ebook and a separate unabridged audiobook. The audiobook runs for 4 hours 5 minutes and is AI-narrated by Martin from Google.

faqs.question: Which editions can I choose?
faqs.answer: PDF and EPUB downloads are on itch.io. Google Play has an ebook and a separate audiobook edition.

faqs.question: How long is the Google Play audiobook?
faqs.answer: The unabridged Google Play audiobook runs for 4 hours 5 minutes. It is AI-narrated by Martin from Google.

faqs.question: Who is Austin Crowd?
faqs.answer: Austin is a private investigator who notices patterns but often draws the wrong conclusions. The story begins when he intercepts a sealed packet connected to Article 18.

book-toknight-2.intro: ToKnight 2: The Fire Beneath is the second book in the Jason Proud series. Jason, Kiera and Angus find an ancient door beneath their school library and a wounded dragon below it, while a new student takes a dangerous interest in Jason's family name.

details.heading: The Jason Proud series
details.text: An ordinary Australian Year Six student has enough to deal with before spectral ancestors and dragons get involved. The Jason Proud series follows the responsibility and kindness that courage asks of him.

details.heading: A middle-grade fantasy sequel
details.text: Recommended for readers around ages 8–12 who enjoy dragons, secret magic and school adventures. Follow the Amazon link for the novel; the itch.io companion page does not offer a book download.

faqs.question: Where does this book fit in the Jason Proud series?
faqs.answer: The Fire Beneath is the second Jason Proud book. Start with ToKnight for his first adventure.

faqs.question: Who might enjoy it?
faqs.answer: Readers around ages 8–12 who like dragons, secret magic, school adventures and funny fantasy with heart.

book-free-to-a-good-home.intro: Free to a Good Home is a contemporary Australian young-adult mystery-drama about fifteen-year-old Tom, who meets Jonah during a family holiday at a caravan park. Jonah is a watchful boy with no clear story about who is meant to be caring for him, and Tom finds it increasingly difficult to ignore the gaps around him.

details.heading: A mystery about noticing
details.text: Tom is already frustrated by the holiday and the responsibilities around his younger brother Max when Jonah appears. As Tom begins to notice what the adults are missing, questions about family, responsibility and safety become harder to ignore.

details.heading: Where to read it
details.text: Read the novel on Amazon. The itch.io page introduces the story and links to Amazon, but does not offer a book download.

faqs.question: What is the story about?
faqs.answer: During a family holiday, Tom notices Jonah, a boy who seems to be appearing in places where adults should be looking after him. The story follows Tom's growing concern and the question of what responsibility asks of him.

faqs.question: Is it available as an itch.io download?
faqs.answer: No. The itch.io page introduces the book; follow its Amazon link to read it.

updates.dateMeaning: Release date shown on the author's book page
updates.title: Free to a Good Home released
updates.summary: Free to a Good Home was released on Amazon on 3 May 2026.

book-a-place-of-his-own.intro: A Place of His Own is a quiet Australian young-adult novel and a sequel to Free to a Good Home. Seven years after Jonah was found at a caravan park, he is nearly seventeen and his living arrangement has become uncertain; the Walsh family must consider how to help without deciding his future for him.

details.heading: A sequel about listening
details.text: Tom, Max and Jonah are at different stages of growing up. Family, disability, communication and guilt shape the choices around them, but caring for Jonah means listening to him rather than deciding where he belongs.

details.heading: Intended readers
details.text: Contemporary Australian young-adult fiction, recommended for ages 13–17. Check Amazon for current availability: the older itch.io page still contains both preorder and released wording.

faqs.question: Should I read Free to a Good Home first?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Place of His Own is a sequel to Free to a Good Home. The earlier novel tells the story of how Jonah was found and introduced to the Walsh family.

faqs.question: Who is it for?
faqs.answer: Recommended for readers aged 13–17.

book-colossal.intro: Colossal is an adult historical tragedy set in ancient Rome. Aurelius is an enslaved gladiator whose victories make him valuable to the people who own him; behind the champion's public image, he studies the arena and begins turning his fame into a chance to resist.

details.heading: Survival under the spectacle
details.text: Aurelius protects a young recruit, looks for a way out and faces Rome's demand for submission. Survival and revolt become inseparable from his struggle to keep hold of his own identity.

details.heading: Where to read it
details.text: Colossal is adult historical fiction. Follow the Amazon link to read it; the itch.io page is a showcase rather than a downloadable edition.

faqs.question: What kind of story is Colossal?
faqs.answer: It is an adult historical tragedy set in ancient Rome, following an enslaved gladiator's effort to survive and resist the system that owns him.

faqs.question: Where can I read Colossal?
faqs.answer: Follow the Amazon link. The book is not available as an itch.io download.

book-concubine.intro: Concubine is an adult political science-fiction novel about Seren Vale, the former First Minister of Veyra. After an occupying power strips her of office, citizenship and legal identity, Seren is brought back to her home world and begins using the empire's own rituals and assumptions to rebuild resistance.

details.heading: Occupation and resistance
details.text: The Orison Concord occupies Veyra under the language of order and mercy. Behind it stands Aion, an artificial intelligence worshipped as a god, controlling gateways, terraforming systems and civilisation's survival models.

details.heading: Formats and availability
details.text: Paperback and ebook formats are listed. Check Amazon for current availability: the older itch.io page still has preorder wording alongside a Released status.

faqs.question: Who is Seren Vale?
faqs.answer: Seren was Veyra's First Minister before the Orison Concord invaded. After losing her public identity and legal personhood, she returns under occupation and begins rebuilding resistance.

faqs.question: Which formats can I look for?
faqs.answer: Paperback and ebook. Check Amazon for current availability, as the older itch.io page contains conflicting preorder and released wording.

book-sober.seoTitle: Sober novel set after the Drink game
book-sober.intro: Sober is a novel that continues the narrative world of the game Drink six months after its ending. Told through alternating perspectives, it follows Drink and Sober as they live separate, structured lives in the same city while memories of the past surface in ordinary moments.

details.heading: Two lives moving forward
details.text: Drink lives in a rented room and works a routine job; Sober works long shifts in a pharmacy. Their lives unfold through small observations and sparse dialogue, with the past returning in ordinary moments.

details.heading: Reading formats
details.text: The Amazon announcement included Kindle, paperback and hardcover editions, alongside a free or small-donation download on itch.io. Check Amazon for the editions currently available.

faqs.question: How is the novel related to the game Drink?
faqs.answer: It continues six months after the game's ending. Drink returns, and Sober brings a second perspective as their stories move forward separately.

faqs.question: Which reading formats were announced?
faqs.answer: The announcement included Kindle, paperback and hardcover editions on Amazon, plus a free or small-donation option on itch.io.

updates.dateMeaning: Publication date of the author's announcement that Sober was available on Amazon
updates.title: Sober announced for Amazon editions
updates.summary: I announced Sober on Amazon in Kindle, paperback and hardcover editions, with a free or small-donation option on itch.io.

details.heading: Track listing
details.text: The nine tracks are The Day, The Pub, The Regular, The Hotel, The Sommelier, The Night, The Cabaret, The Emcee and The End.

details.heading: Listen on Spotify
details.text: Listen to Drink (Original Soundtrack) on Spotify.

faqs.question: How many tracks are on the album?
faqs.answer: Nine tracks.

music-billions-of-years.intro: Billions of Years is my ten-track album, including “You Don't Hear Me,” “Macca's Chai at Midnight,” “Borrowed Home” and the title track. “You Don't Hear Me” is marked explicit on Spotify.

details.heading: Track listing
details.text: The ten tracks are You Don't Hear Me, In a Tree, Macca's Chai at Midnight, Bad Luck, Pause and Play, Flinder Bop, Permission to Fall, Borrowed Home, Good Life Anyway and Billions of Years.

details.heading: Listen on Spotify
details.text: Listen to Billions of Years on Spotify.

faqs.question: Which tracks are on the album?
faqs.answer: There are ten tracks, from “You Don't Hear Me” through “Billions of Years.” “You Don't Hear Me” is marked explicit on Spotify.

music-tower-defense-pack-ost.intro: Samfa12's Tower Defense Pack brings together 19 tracks, including music named for Ship Blockade, Bug Maze TD, Coop Guard TD and Library Lockdown TD, plus the pack's menu track.

details.heading: Nineteen tracks
details.text: The album includes Tower Defense Pack Main Menu, two Ship Blockade tracks, four Bug Maze TD tracks, six Coop Guard TD tracks and six Library Lockdown TD tracks. The titles do not specify which editions of the games use each track.

details.heading: Listen on Spotify
details.text: Find the album on Spotify as Samfa12's Tower Defense Pack. The Spotify title does not include the OST suffix used here.

faqs.question: How many tracks are on the album?
faqs.answer: Nineteen tracks.

music-lofi-and-chill-pack-ost.intro: Samfa12's Lofi and Chill Pack Original Soundtrack brings together 26 tracks, from “Attic Train Map” and “Blue Hour Bubbles” to pieces named for Moon Mower, Pocket Ant Farm, Pocket Fish Tank and other small-world projects.

details.heading: Twenty-six named pieces
details.text: The 26 tracks include Attic Train Map, Blue Hour Bubbles, Burrow Radio, Clover Tunnel, Moon Mower Original, Pocket Ant Farm Original, Pocket Fish Tank Original, Pocket Koi Pond Original, Pocket Aviary Original, Pocket Train Set Original and Window Seat Rain.

details.heading: Listen on Spotify
details.text: Listen on Spotify under Samfa12's Lofi and Chill Pack Original Soundtrack. Track names do not specify exactly where a piece appears in a game.

faqs.question: How many tracks are on the album?
faqs.answer: Twenty-six tracks.

book-dust-on-the-river.intro: Dust on the River is an Australian historical novel based on the Samfa12 videogame. In a fictional north-east Victorian river town in the early 1890s, a newcomer hopes steady work will let him leave a bushranger past behind.

details.heading: A new name in Crossing
details.text: Caleb Reed arrives by train and begins to earn trust through stock work and practical help. Around him are river country, goldfield rumours and people who know more about his past than he wants to admit. The longer Amazon description includes later story details if you want to know more.

details.heading: The book and the game
details.text: This novel is based on the Dust on the River videogame. The book has Kindle and paperback editions on Amazon; the separate game has browser and Android destinations. The Kindle edition has a listed publication date of 1 September 2026.

faqs.question: Is this the Dust on the River game?
faqs.answer: No. This is the novel based on the game. The game has a separate page, play destinations and platform information.

faqs.question: Which book editions are shown on Amazon Australia?
faqs.answer: Kindle and paperback are listed. Check Amazon for current edition availability and prices.

book-the-wall-that-lied.intro: The Wall that Lied opens The Broken Road trilogy. Military engineer Tomas Parker saved Auster by bringing down the King’s Road during an invasion, but the cost made him a hated figure. Twenty-one years later, an enemy returns and the city’s defences may rest on a falsehood.

details.heading: Siege and engineering
details.text: Parker is called back to defend Auster while the past and his estranged family remain unresolved. Siege warfare, engineering and political pressure force decisions with a human cost.

details.heading: First in The Broken Road
details.text: This is Book 1 of 3 in The Broken Road. No Wall to Hold follows as Book 2, and What We Save closes the trilogy.

faqs.question: Where does this book sit in the trilogy?
faqs.answer: The Wall that Lied is Book 1 of 3 in The Broken Road, followed by No Wall to Hold and What We Save.

faqs.question: Where can I get the Kindle edition?
faqs.answer: View the Kindle edition on Amazon Australia for current purchase information.

book-no-wall-to-hold.intro: No Wall to Hold is the second Broken Road book. After the defence of Auster, engineer Tomas Parker must move a grain convoy through a damaged political landscape while refugees, soldiers and villages join the road.

details.heading: A defence that has to move
details.text: The campaign moves from a city wall to roads, bridges and the people depending on them. Supplies, authority and promises become harder to manage as the column grows in this adult low-fantasy story of logistics and consequences.

details.heading: Second in The Broken Road
details.text: This is Book 2 of 3 in The Broken Road. The Kindle edition is available on Amazon Australia.

faqs.question: Should I read The Wall that Lied first?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Wall that Lied is Book 1, and No Wall to Hold is Book 2. The first book covers the preceding events at Auster and Parker’s earlier choice.

faqs.question: Has the Kindle edition been released?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Kindle edition is available on Amazon Australia.

book-what-we-save.intro: What We Save concludes The Broken Road trilogy. Tomas Parker returns to a threatened Auster with refugees, wounded soldiers and grain, as the city faces another choice about who and what its defences protect.

details.heading: The closing Auster campaign
details.text: Parker returns to the capital under the pressure of siege warfare, engineering problems, political conflict and morally difficult decisions. This adult low-fantasy story follows a city whose survival depends on more than its walls.

details.heading: Third in The Broken Road
details.text: This is Book 3 of 3 in The Broken Road. At the 23 September 2026 check, Amazon Australia offered the Kindle edition for preorder with delivery scheduled for 1 December 2026. Check Amazon for current availability.

faqs.question: Is this the last book in The Broken Road?
faqs.answer: Yes. What We Save is Book 3 of 3, following The Wall that Lied and No Wall to Hold.

faqs.question: When is the Kindle edition scheduled?
faqs.answer: The Kindle edition was scheduled for 1 December 2026 when Amazon Australia was checked on 23 September. Check Amazon for current availability.
